items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: he'd go upstairs and blew all the money in a crap game with Charlie Glenn and Joe Ziggy Johnson

ctx.x: All right. T-Bone would get on the show and they'd throw all kinds -- twenty-dollar bills, I was pretty honest -- boy from Texas -- on me, and I took up the change and the bills every day and I'd meet him backstage and I was director of the show, and give him all his money; he'd give me ten dollars, which was good. I mean, I'm doing this every show. But he'd go upstairs
and blew all the money in a crap game with Charlie Glenn and Joe Ziggy Johnson and I found this out and I said, "No kiddin'".

So I started taking me some money, Helen. So I was making off of T-Bone. He'd lay down with me some good money — I'd hang out in the evening and put that guitar and make that lickety-split, "In the evening, baby when the sun goes down, doo doo doo, and they'd scream "Wow" and throw that money down there ... from the balcony and everywhere.
